title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Executive and non-executive directors of Starpharma and its subsidiaries. Distinguished for approval routing (Chairman, or Board for the Chairman's own dealings) and a mandatory immediate post-trade confirmation to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: The CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, key management personnel (excluding Directors), direct reports of the CEO, of the CFO & Company Secretary, and of the VP Development & Regulatory Affairs, and any other employee designated by the Company Secretary in consultation with the CEO.

tiers.name: Employees (excluding Designated Persons and Directors)
tiers.description: All other employees of and contractors to Starpharma and its subsidiaries. Only 48 hours' prior notice to the Company Secretary is required to deal; no approval or discretion to refuse is described for this tier.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Family members, friends and companies or other entities controlled by the Employee or their family members. The Employee must take reasonable steps to prevent an associate dealing in a way that would breach the policy if done by the Employee, and must give the required notice or seek the required approval on the associate's behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: any transaction which would have the effect of hedging or otherwise transferring to any other person the risk of any fluctuation in the value of: (a) Securities in the Company which are subject to a restriction on disposal under an employee share or incentive plan; or (b) Options or performance rights (or any unvested securities in the Company underlying them)

windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Company's annual results
24 hours after the release of the Company's half-year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company Secretary or an authorised delegate may declare 'Any other period communicated to you' as a further Prohibited Period, notified by email; the policy does not state whether the existence or reason for such a period is confidential.

rules.detail: Outside a Prohibited Period, non-designated Employees may deal in Starpharma securities or derivative products merely by giving 48 hours' notice to the Company Secretary; there is no approval or discretion to refuse described for this tier. Trading in 'derivative products' is expressly banned during Prohibited Periods.
rules.evidence: trading in Starpharma securities or derivative products is not permitted during the following periods

rules.detail: Designated Persons must give notice of intention to deal and receive written approval from the CEO and Company Secretary before dealing in securities or derivative products, and are barred outright during a Prohibited Period absent exceptional-circumstances consent.
rules.evidence: All Designated Persons must give notice to the CEO and Company Secretary of their intention to deal in securities of Starpharma prior to dealing.

rules.detail: Directors (other than the Chairman) need Chairman/CEO/Company Secretary approval; the Chairman needs Board approval. Both must give 48 hours' notice before dealing, are barred during Prohibited Periods absent exceptional-circumstances consent, and must give immediate post-trade confirmation to the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: Directors must give at least 48 hours’ notice to the Chairman, the CEO and Company Secretary of their intention to deal in securities of Starpharma prior to dealing.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging or transferring the risk of value fluctuation in Securities that remain subject to a disposal restriction under an employee share or incentive plan.
rules.evidence: Employees may not enter into any transaction which would have the effect of hedging or otherwise transferring to any other person the risk of any fluctuation in the value of: (a) Securities in the Company which are subject to a restriction on disposal under an employee share or incentive plan

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging options, performance rights, or unvested securities underlying them. Key management personnel (including Directors) and their closely related parties face an additional, separate statutory hedging ban under the Corporations Act 2001.
rules.evidence: Options or performance rights (or any unvested securities in the Company underlying them) (“Hedging Transactions”).

rules.detail: Hedging vested shares no longer subject to a plan disposal restriction is not a defined 'Hedging Transaction' and so is not banned by 3(g). An OTC put/call over such shares is nonetheless a dealing in an 'other financial product' caught by the general notification (non-designated Employees) or approval (Designated Persons/Directors) regime and the Prohibited Period ban.
rules.evidence: Securities include: ... any other financial products traded on ASX.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures such as a prepaid forward are not named. Such an arrangement is an 'other financial product' and an agreement to sell securities, so it is a Dealing requiring notification or approval and is banned in a Prohibited Period; a structure that grants security over the shares would also need to be checked against the margin loan ban.
rules.evidence: It extends to exercising options over securities and entering agreements to buy or sell securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not named. Selling Starpharma securities is a Dealing subject to the same notification/approval and Prohibited Period rules; the policy is silent on whether borrowing stock to sell short is itself restricted, as stock lending is not addressed.
rules.evidence: Dealing in securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending by the Employee (as lender) is not named anywhere in the policy and is not listed as a form of Dealing.
CFDs are not named. They are 'other financial products' and so a Dealing requiring notification or approval, subject to the Prohibited Period ban and the three-month short-term dealing restriction.
rules.evidence: any other financial products traded on ASX

rules.detail: Outright ban, defined broadly to include any facility secured by Starpharma securities where the lender may sell, or the client may be required to sell, shares to reduce the loan-to-value ratio. Applies regardless of vesting state and to all Employees, a defined term that includes Directors.
rules.evidence: Margin loan arrangements must not be entered into by Employees. ... a facility that provides for the borrowing of money against the value of Starpharma securities, where the loan is secured by those Starpharma securities, and the lender may be entitled, or the client may be required, to dispose of some of the Starpharma securities to reduce the loan-to-value ratio of the facility.

rules.detail: A 'bona fide mortgage' over Starpharma securities is expressly excluded from the concept of Dealing, so pledging vested shares as loan security is not itself subject to the general notification/approval or Prohibited Period regime, provided the facility does not also meet the definition of a banned 'margin loan arrangement' (loan-to-value-triggered forced sale) under 3(f).
rules.evidence: It extends to exercising options over securities and entering agreements to buy or sell securities, but does not include a bona fide mortgage over the securities.

rules.detail: Only 'margin loan arrangements' are banned, defined narrowly as a facility secured by Starpharma securities where the lender may (or the client must) sell shares to maintain the loan-to-value ratio. A secured loan without that loan-to-value/forced-sale feature is not expressly captured by this clause, though the initial charge and any eventual sale still fall to be checked against the bona-fide-mortgage carve-out and the general Dealing regime.
rules.evidence: a facility that provides for the borrowing of money against the value of Starpharma securities, where the loan is secured by those Starpharma securities, and the lender may be entitled, or the client may be required, to dispose of some of the Starpharma securities to reduce the loan-to-value ratio of the facility.

rules.detail: No buying and selling (or selling and buying) Starpharma securities within a three-month period, and no other short-term dealings, without written permission from the Company Secretary (in consultation with the CEO).
rules.evidence: Employees may not: buy and sell (or sell and buy) Starpharma securities within a three-month period without written permission from the Company Secretary (in consultation with the CEO); or enter into any other short-term dealings in Starpharma securities without written permission from the Company Secretary (in consultation with the CEO).

rules.detail: Selling shares acquired under an employee incentive scheme within three months of acquisition is expressly carved out of the short-term dealing ban, but the sale still requires notification (non-designated Employees) or approval (Designated Persons/Directors) under 3(c)/(d).
rules.evidence: The sale of shares which have been acquired as a result of an employee incentive scheme operated by Starpharma within three months of being acquired is not considered short term dealing, however remains subject to the notification and approval procedures detailed in clauses 3(c) and (d) (as appropriate).

clearance.evidence: you are permitted to trade in Starpharma securities without prior approval provided you have given at least 48 hours’ notice to the Company Secretary prior to trading, you are not in possession of inside information and your trades are conducted in accordance with this policy.

All Designated Persons must give notice to the CEO and Company Secretary of their intention to deal in securities of Starpharma prior to dealing. You will receive a written response within 48 hours of the request and if approved, will outline the duration of the consent.

clearance.approver: Chairman, CEO and Company Secretary (Board, in consultation with the CEO and another non-executive director, for the Chairman's own dealings)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (identity, number, price and nature of the trade)
clearance.evidence: Directors must give at least 48 hours’ notice to the Chairman, the CEO and Company Secretary of their intention to deal ... All Directors must give immediate notice to the Company Secretary following any dealing by them or an associate in securities of Starpharma.

carve_outs: sale of shares acquired under an employee incentive scheme within three months of acquisition (still subject to the notification/approval procedures)
short_term.evidence: Employees may not: buy and sell (or sell and buy) Starpharma securities within a three-month period without written permission from the Company Secretary (in consultation with the CEO); or enter into any other short-term dealings in Starpharma securities without written permission from the Company Secretary (in consultation with the CEO).

exceptions.evidence: acquiring securities as a result of: an offer under an employee incentive scheme operated by Starpharma; or a performance share right vesting, exercising options or converting convertible securities.
investing or trading in a fund or scheme where the investment decisions are made by a third party, provided that the fund or scheme does not invest solely in Starpharma securities
trading in securities by a relevant trustee (who is not also a beneficiary of the trust) and the decision to trade is made by other trustees or investment managers independent of that person
undertaking to accept, or accepting, a takeover offer or scheme of arrangement

exceptions.approver: Board (approves timing and structure of the plan)
exceptions.evidence: trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most security holders, including dividend reinvestment plans, share purchase plans, rights issues and equal access buy-backs, where the timing and structure of the plan has been approved by the Board

exceptions.approver: Company Secretary (in consultation with the CEO); Chairman for Directors; Board for the Chairman
exceptions.evidence: financial hardship which cannot reasonably be alleviated other than by dealing in securities of Starpharma

exceptions.approver: Company Secretary (in consultation with the CEO); Chairman for Directors; Board for the Chairman
exceptions.evidence: a court order directing the dealing in securities of Starpharma

exemption_authority: Trading in a Prohibited Period may only be permitted for financial hardship or a court order, for a consent lasting no more than 5 trading days; Employees apply to the Company Secretary (with the CEO), Designated Persons to the CEO or Company Secretary, Directors to the Chairman, and the Chairman to the Board. Outside Prohibited Periods, clearance to trade may be given or refused by Starpharma in its discretion, without giving reasons, and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light.

bespoke_clauses.clause: does not include a bona fide mortgage over the securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A genuine security interest granted over vested shares that does not replicate the margin loan definition's loan-to-value/forced-sale mechanic may fall outside the 'Dealing' concept entirely, potentially letting the loan leg of a collar be documented without clearance or Prohibited Period restriction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a facility that provides for the borrowing of money against the value of Starpharma securities, where the loan is secured by those Starpharma securities, and the lender may be entitled, or the client may be required, to dispose of some of the Starpharma securities to reduce the loan-to-value ratio of the facility.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares with any loan-to-value top-up or forced-sale right is squarely banned as a margin loan; the facility must be structured without that feature to avoid the outright prohibition in 3(f).

bespoke_clauses.clause: key management personnel (including Directors) and their closely related parties are prohibited from entering into Hedging Transactions by the Corporations Act 2001.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for vested, unrestricted holdings, KMP and their closely related parties (a wider class than the policy's own 'associate') face a separate statutory hedging ban that must be checked independently of this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If it is not a Prohibited Period, unless you are a Designated Person or Director, you are permitted to trade in Starpharma securities without prior approval provided you have given at least 48 hours’ notice
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Executives eligible for a collar are almost always Designated Persons or Directors, so in practice they face a discretionary, refusable approval regime rather than the lighter notice-only regime available to rank-and-file employees.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if clearance to trade is refused, you must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank counterparty cannot be told why a collar clearance was refused, which complicates diligence and timing certainty for trade execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities include: ... any other financial products traded on ASX.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The formal 'Securities' definition is limited to ASX-traded products, but the standalone Prohibited Period ban on 'derivative products' has no such limit; treat an OTC-only put/call collar as caught out of caution given the express, unqualified reference to derivative products.

summary: A funded collar is achievable in outline but constrained on the financing side. The derivative legs (purchased put, written call) over vested, unrestricted shares are not 'Hedging Transactions' under 3(g) (which only catches plan-restricted or unvested securities), so they are a Dealing in a financial product permitted with CEO/Company Secretary approval for Directors and Designated Persons, outside the three Prohibited Periods, and only while not in possession of inside information. The loan leg is harder: Starpharma bans any 'margin loan arrangement', defined as a facility secured by Starpharma shares where the lender can force a sale to maintain a loan-to-value ratio, so a conventionally LVR-managed collar loan is prohibited outright; a bona fide mortgage without that forced-sale feature is arguably outside both the ban and the Dealing concept, but this is an untested reading requiring careful drafting. Key management personnel and their closely related parties also face a standalone statutory hedging ban under the Corporations Act that must be cleared independently of the policy. Tenor should exceed three months, and entry, unwind or roll of the collar all need fresh approval and must sit outside a Prohibited Period absent hardship or court-order relief capped at five trading days.
